title: Write a scale of 1 cm to k km in the form 1 to n
source: Theory IGCSE-15.1 Quick check 1 (1 cm to 8 km gives n=800000); book scale-ratio work on printed pp.472–473, new numbers
stem: A map uses a scale of 1 cm to {k|int} km. When this scale of the map is written as \(1:n\), what is the value of \(n\)?

steps.name: A
steps.note: N is k times 100000. Original: 8 km = 800000 cm.

title: Convert a real length to a length on a scale drawing
source: Theory IGCSE-15.1 Quick check 2 (40 m at 1 cm to 4 m gives 10 cm); book Worked example 1 style, new numbers
stem: A path is {L|int} m long. It is shown on a scale drawing that uses a scale of 1 cm to {s|int} m. What is the length, in centimetres, of the path on the drawing?

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: Divide the real length by the number of metres represented by 1 cm: \({L|int}\div {s|int}={D|int}\).
steps.note: D is L/s and is an integer by the constraint. Original: 40/4=10.

title: Convert a length on a scale drawing to a real length
source: Theory IGCSE-15.1 Quick check 3 (12 cm at 1 cm to 5 m gives 60 m); book conversion work on printed pp.472–473, new numbers
stem: The height of a tower is {c|int} cm on a scale drawing that uses a scale of 1 cm to {s|int} m. What is the actual height of the tower, in metres?

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: Multiply the length on the drawing by the number of metres represented by 1 cm: \({c|int}\times {s|int}={H|int}\).
steps.note: H is c times s. Original: 12 times 5 = 60.

title: Actual distance from a map length and a scale 1 to 50000

source.note: Stem taken from the QP PDF (UCLES 2023), Question 8(b) only. Official answer and mark allocation from the MS PDF. The item is paper/self-mark. Parts 8(a) and 8(c)–(d) are omitted (construction, a measurement, angle chasing, and Pythagoras).

stem:
This question is 0580/32/O/N/23 Question 8(b), taken from the official QP.

(b) Town \(A\) is 8.5 cm from town \(B\) on a map.
The scale of the map is \(1 : 50\,000\).

Calculate the actual distance from town \(A\) to town \(B\).
Give your answer in kilometres.  [2]

steps.name: M
steps.text_tex: 8.5 cm represents \(8.5\times 50000=425000\) cm, which is 4250 m, or 4.25 km. Equivalently, 1 cm represents 0.5 km, so the distance is \(8.5\times 0.5=4.25\) km.
steps.note: Official MS 8(b): 4.25 for 2 marks, with B1 for figures 425 as the answer or 1 cm = 0.5 km seen, or M1 for 8.5 x 50000 oe. This step records the official M1 route, which is the method written here. Independent: 8.5 times 50000 cm = 425000 cm = 4.25 km.

steps.name: A
steps.note: Official MS 8(b): 4.25 for 2 marks. Independent confirmation: 4.25 km.
